picks.headline: "The hypocrisy in the industry is insane": Todd Edwards on sampling Suno
picks.excerpt: House/UKG producer Todd Edwards says he now generates his own material in Suno Studio to sample and chop, calling it a co-producer that frees him from sample-clearance lawsuits, and calls industry criticism hypocritical.
picks.rationale: A concrete producer workflow: a veteran sampling artist generates his own Suno Studio material to chop, sidestepping clearance. New angle vs recent Suno v6 deal/lawsuit cards.

picks.headline: Backgrounds creates soundscapes from keyword prompts
picks.excerpt: Sampleson Backgrounds uses semantic audio retrieval over 22,000 audio cells and 11,000 local embeddings to build evolving soundscapes from keywords dragged onto a canvas; runs locally.
picks.rationale: New local, subscription-free tool that builds soundscapes from keyword prompts via embeddings; actionable for sound designers.

picks.headline: IMPF and IMPEL publish AI licensing principles
picks.excerpt: Independent publisher bodies IMPF and IMPEL publish a generative-AI licensing framework whose non-negotiable principle is that songs be valued at least equally with recordings, plus transparency on training vs output payments.
picks.rationale: Fresh licensing framework from indie publishers setting song-vs-master parity for AI deals; strongest of 4 same-story outlets (CMU chosen, Music Ally/MBW/DMN set aside).

picks.headline: Absolute opens AI-powered Anthology Music OS
picks.excerpt: Absolute Label Services opens its AI-powered Anthology 'Music OS' with in-house LLM Ant to indie rights holders; Cherry Red and Blue Raincoat are first customers.
picks.rationale: Non-generative AI applied to label operations (in-house LLM across distribution, royalties, reporting) now opened to indies.

picks.headline: Appeals court rejects fair use defense over AI training
picks.excerpt: US Third Circuit upholds that Ross Intelligence's copying of Westlaw material for AI training was not fair use; RIAA and NMPA backed Thomson Reuters, framing it as precedent for Suno/Udio cases.
picks.rationale: First appellate ruling rejecting fair use for AI training, backed by RIAA/NMPA with direct implications for the Suno and Udio cases.
